summary: Jules Mohl worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Sinology. He studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy and Abel-Rémusat. He became a professor at Tübingen (1826) and later Professor des Persischen at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Jules Oppert was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at the Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums and the universities of Heidelberg, Bonn, Berlin, and Kiel. From 1874 to 1905, he served as a professor at the Collège de France.

Julia Ching was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University. She later held a post at the University of Toronto (~1978–2001).

Julia F. Andrews specializes in Sinology and history and archaeology. She completed her studies at Brown University, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University. She took up a post at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie worked in Indology and religious studies. She founded SOAS University of London and later held an academic post there from approximately 1993 to 2004.

Julian Strube is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at Heidelberg (2015–2019), Amsterdam (2016–2017), the University of Münster (2019–2021), and the University of Vienna (~2021).

Juliane Schober specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies, earning her PhD from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989. She was attested as an Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Arizona State University in 2007.

Julie A. Gifford specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under the supervision of Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.

Julius Eggeling was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1869–1875) and taught Sanskrit at University College London and the University of Edinburgh (~1875–1914).

Julius Euting specialized in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Eberhard-Ludwigs-Gymnasium, the Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the BNU de Strasbourg (~1871–1909) and the University of Strasbourg (~1880–1912).

Julius Grill was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen and under Rudolf von Roth and Adalbert Kuhn. He held professorships at the Seminaries of Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1874–1904) and Tübingen (1888).

Julius Jolly was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin under Albrecht Weber and also under Martin Haug. From 1872 to 1923, he held posts at the University of Würzburg, becoming Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology in 1886.

Julius Lipner is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. He studied at King's College London, Clare Hall, Cambridge, and the University of Birmingham. He held posts at the University of Birmingham (~1974–1975) and the University of Cambridge (~1975).

Jun Fujii is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo (~2000–2006). He held a post as a full-time lecturer at Komazawa University from around 2008 to 2013.

Jun Takashima specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and at Kyoto University. He later held posts at Aichi Prefectural University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, where he was a professor (2002–2021).

Jundo Nagashima is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University and the University of Bristol under Paul Williams, Alexis Sanderson, and Seitatsu Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2006–2017).

June McDaniel is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned an MTS at Emory University and a PhD at the University of Chicago. She served as Professor of the History of Religions at the College of Charleston (attested 2000, 2015).

Junglan Bang is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Dongguk University, trained under Seung-suk Jung and Sungdoo Ahn, and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2012) under Harunaga Isaacson, later visiting Kyoto University as a researcher.

Jungmin Ha specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Ha completed a master's degree at Seoul National University under Juhyung Rhi and earned a PhD from Duke University under Stanley Abe (attested 2016).

Junjirō Takakusu was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku, Tokyo, and Oxford, learning under Max Müller, Winternitz, and Lévi. He held posts at Tokyo, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University of Foreign Studies, and Toyo University.
